clue.text: H is for icing on the cake

definitions.meaning: the letter H ends the word touch, so it is literally the closing letter that touch receives
the extra flourish that completes something already good

explanation.surface: A dictionary-style entry explaining what the letter H stands for in a cake-decorating glossary.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing on the cake is an idiom for the final detail that perfects a piece of work.

clue.text: Same touch in disguise?

parts.note: these two words are what a fake, or rearranged, version of the facial-hair word looks like: its letters shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone notices the same small detail turning up in a disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: FALSE is an anagram signal and MOUSTACHE its fodder, which rearranges to SAME TOUCH. The answer is also literally a disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: A stick-on whisker set is the classic way to disguise a face, as in any comic spy story.

clue.text: Many gentle types show lack of attention

indicators.note: types read as a verb meaning sorts into kinds, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: C, the Roman numeral for a hundred, stands for many

explanation.surface: A great number of mild-mannered people are seen to be inattentive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'types' reorganises C (many) with GENTLE to give NEGLECT.
explanation.definitionFit: Neglect is failure to give proper care or attention, so it is a lack of attention as a noun.

clue.text: Fixers in flight for 15, Dior fashion

indicators.note: fashion as a verb means to shape or form, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: refers to the answer at 15 across, a word for celebrities or heavenly bodies

explanation.surface: Celebrities get kitted out by the fashion house Dior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' rearranges STARS (the answer to 15 across) plus DIOR into STAIR RODS. A flight here is a flight of stairs, not air travel.
explanation.definitionFit: Stair rods are metal bars that hold a carpet in place on each step of a staircase.

clue.text: Reactionary tendency of a tier in administration

indicators.note: administration here means management or handling, so the letters are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A political tier of government is slow to change once installed in office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'administration' rearranges A TIER IN into INERTIA.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics inertia is a body's resistance to change in motion, a tendency to react against force.

clue.text: 1 across could be gaudy, if lacking heart

definitions.text: 1 across could be gaudy, if lacking heart

parts.words: 1 across could be gaudy, if lacking heart
parts.note: a final decorative touch for food, whose seven letters lose their central N to leave a word for flashy or gaudy

explanation.surface: A decorative flourish might look vulgar if it has no soul behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 across is FINISHING TOUCH, defining the answer; drop the middle letter N and GARISH (gaudy) remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A garnish is a decoration added to a dish as its final flourish before serving.

clue.text: The sultan was a great guy

parts.note: OS is the abbreviation for outsize, a clothing label for large sizes
a guy is a man

explanation.surface: A historical sultan is praised as having been a fine fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Osman I founded the Ottoman dynasty and was its first sultan, the empire being named after him.

clue.text: Taken short, state needs a toilet after West Indian greens

parts.note: the state of California taken in shortened form gives CAL
loo is British slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: A desperate traveller, caught short, wants a lavatory after eating Caribbean vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: Being taken short is a British idiom for urgently needing a toilet; here it means the state's name is cut down.
explanation.definitionFit: Calaloo is a leafy vegetable, and the soup made from it, eaten across the Caribbean.

clue.text: You are owners of a gift shop

definitions.meaning: the people here now, as in the phrase excepting those who are here
a business whose goods are gifts, read playfully as a firm dealing in presents

explanation.surface: A quiz question about who runs the local souvenir shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Present company means the people who are here, the listeners addressed as you.

clue.text: It's carried on a sleigh (wherein is a joke)

indicators.note: wherein is says the joke sits inside the sleigh

parts.note: a luge is a small racing sledge
a gag is a joke

explanation.surface: Something is carried on a sledge, with a little humour tucked in the parentheses.
explanation.definitionFit: Luggage is the baggage a traveller carries, the cases and bags taken on a journey.

clue.text: One who might incur blame going round in a posh car ?

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the car's abbreviation

parts.note: RR is short for a Rolls-Royce, the archetypal luxury car

indicators.note: going round suggests turning in circles, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who drives around in a Rolls-Royce might attract criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: RR (Rolls-Royce) is the standard crossword posh car; the words 'who might incur' only link the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A rambler is one who walks for pleasure, a person defined by the word one.

clue.text: Retreating soldiers cover leading Egyptian officer

indicators.note: cover means the soldiers enclose the letter
retreating means the soldiers' letters are read backwards

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

indicators.note: leading picks the first letter of Egyptian

explanation.surface: Withdrawing troops protect a high-ranking Egyptian commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retreating' turns REME into EMER, which wraps around E.
explanation.definitionFit: An emeer, or emir, is a Muslim ruler or commander, an officer of rank.

clue.text: Girls' neat figures?

indicators.note: figures read as working out, so the letters are recalculated into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark about the tidy shapes of some young women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figures' rearranges the letters of GIRLS NEAT into TRIANGLES, which are themselves neat figures in geometry.
explanation.definitionFit: Triangles are three-sided geometric figures, neat shapes in the mathematical sense.

clue.text: Manipulator hates to trouble about work

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the anagram goes round the work
to trouble means to disturb, so the letters are stirred up

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone who manipulates others loathes being bothered over their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' turns HATES TO into OSTEATH, and 'about' places it round OP.
explanation.definitionFit: An osteopath treats patients by manipulating bones and muscles.

clue.text: Add 1 across to a party of sailors…

parts.note: a do is a party
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to put a final flourish on a party for a ship's crew.
explanation.definitionFit: To adorn is to decorate, giving something its finishing touch as 1 across says.

clue.text: Relative loses time gathering fruit — a mindless worker

indicators.note: gathering means collecting inside, so the relative surrounds the fruit
loses means the time letter is dropped

parts.note: an aunt is a relative
a tomato is botanically a fruit

explanation.surface: A family member stops wasting time picking fruit and works without thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relative' could be many kin, but only one loses a T neatly; 'gathering' is the container signal, the relative enclosing the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: An automaton is a robot, or a person acting mechanically without thought.

clue.text: … sailor aboard takes a lead

annotationWithheld.why: '… sailor aboard takes a lead (5)': the only parse is TAR inside SS, with 'aboard' giving SS and also signalling the insertion, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Obliquely request an Anglican

parts.note: to request is to ask
CE is the Church of England, the Anglican church

explanation.surface: A churchgoer is approached with a sideways appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Askance means with a sidelong glance, looking at something indirectly or obliquely.

clue.text: Cunningly planned distribution of cigarettes (not English)

indicators.note: distribution of means the letters are spread out in a new order
not means the English letter is left out

explanation.surface: A clever scheme to hand out smokes, excluding the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' drops one E from CIGARETTES, and 'distribution of' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Strategic describes something planned with a long-term aim, cunningly thought out.

clue.text: Pointed 15

parts.note: a constellation, with 15 standing for stars, whose name in Latin means arrow, a pointed thing

explanation.surface: Sharp-tipped celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagitta is a small northern constellation named the Arrow.

clue.text: Deterioration reported beneath a building

parts.note: rot is decay or deterioration

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so a word that sounds the same is used

parts.note: beneath means under, said in a non-rhotic accent

explanation.surface: Decay is found under a building.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent UNDER and UNDA sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a round building, typically domed.

clue.text: See sign giving origin

indicators.note: giving means yielding, so the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: Look at the signpost that shows where things began.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis means the beginning or origin of something, as in the first book of the Bible.

clue.text: 18th century spin doctor?

parts.note: not a political adviser but a Georgian inventor who transformed the spinning of cotton

explanation.surface: A Georgian political publicist.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Arkwright patented the water frame for spinning cotton in 1769.

clue.text: Demolish, they say, or the reverse

indicators.note: they say means spoken aloud, so a word sounding the same is used

parts.note: to raze is to demolish

explanation.surface: A building is to be torn down or built up.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting up or building is the opposite of tearing down, so the reverse of demolish.

clue.text: Note a mere drop of medicine

definitions.meaning: a half note in music, a note value
a tiny unit of fluid measure used in pharmacy, about one drop

explanation.surface: A remark about a small dose of medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: A minim is a musical half note and also a sixtieth of a fluid dram.

clue.text: The sign of spun jute

indicators.note: spun means turned round, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A symbol for a spun jute fibre.
explanation.walkthrough: Jute is not the fibre but a member of the Germanic tribe; HENGIST led the Jutes into Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Hengist was a legendary leader of the Jutes who settled in Kent.

clue.text: She repels Nick with a triumphant laugh

indicators.note: repels means drives back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: Old Nick is the Devil
ha is a triumphant laugh

explanation.surface: A woman fends off a devil with a laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: Natasha is a female name, so she.

clue.text: Many set free by military leader

definitions.text: Many set free by military leader

parts.note: a general is a military leader

indicators.note: free means loosed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A general releases many prisoners.
explanation.definitionFit: A general amnesty frees many prisoners, a pardon granted by an authority.
